one_liner: PUC-Rio Lua 5.5.0 with the yk meta-tracing JIT bolted on; about 1.96x faster than stock Lua 5.5 on a 22-benchmark geomean.
what_it_does: yklua is the reference PUC-Rio Lua 5.5.0 interpreter with yk's run-time tracing JIT retrofitted through USE_YK ifdefs. The language, standard library and C API stay those of stock Lua 5.5. You build it with the ykllvm toolchain through yk-config, and hot loops are then traced and compiled to machine code at run time. It is a research artefact, not a packaged runtime: the README calls it experimental and yk's own docs list it as pre-alpha.
how_it_is_fast: yk is a meta-tracing system. ykllvm embeds the interpreter's own LLVM IR (fat LTO, .llvmbc section) and stackmaps in the binary. A yk_mt_control_point call at the top of luaV_execute counts executions of per-pc YkLocations, which are placed at backward-jump and for-loop heads at parse time and at the entry of functions found to be recursive. Once a location passes YK_HOT_THRESHOLD (131 by default), yk records the interpreter's path through its own IR and compiles that trace. The interpreter is annotated so that traces specialise well: yk_promote on constants, prototype sizes and the pc, yk_idempotent on loads, and yk_unroll on helper loops. Constant-folded traces then remove dispatch, type checks and table lookups, in the same way PyPy's meta-tracing does.
when_to_use: Loop-heavy numeric Lua on Linux x86-64, where gains are largest: Mandelbrot 5.8x, BigLoop 3.9x, spectralnorm 3.4x, Heightmap 3.1x, Sieve 3.0x and NBody 2.9x against stock Lua 5.5.0.
You want a JIT while keeping current PUC Lua 5.5 semantics (integers, 5.4/5.5 features) rather than moving to LuaJIT's Lua 5.1 dialect.

Research or prototyping on meta-tracing: the yk changes are a small set of USE_YK hooks in lvm.c, ldo.c, lparser.c, lfunc.c and lstate.c, so it is a readable worked example of retrofitting a JIT into a C interpreter.
Long-running scripts where a 1.5-2x average speedup is worth carrying an experimental toolchain (Rust nightly, ykllvm).
when_not_to_use: Production or shipped embeddings. The README says experimental, yk's docs rate it pre-alpha, all.lua is 'currently failing for non-serialised compilation', and 25 issues are open, including per-file test failures since 2023 and a lua_assert failure in luac (#110).
Any platform other than Linux on x86-64 (a yk requirement), or builds that cannot use Rust nightly and the ykllvm LLVM fork.
Object-heavy or allocation-heavy code gains little: DeltaBlue 1.09x, Storage 1.23x, Havlak 1.24x, CD 1.35x and binarytrees 1.36x.
Hosts that load Lua C modules or other code with dlopen at run time. yk's gotchas say it assumes no code is loaded or unloaded at run time, and code without embedded IR cannot be inlined into traces.
When peak speed matters more than Lua 5.5 compatibility: the author's 2026 blog post says it does not reach LuaJIT's peak performance (search snippet only; tratt.net is blocked here).

integration.form: source-drop (lua executable and liblua.a built with ykllvm via yk-config)
integration.dependencies: yk runtime (Rust ykcapi library, Apache-2.0 or MIT), ykllvm (yk's LLVM fork, a yk submodule) and GNU make
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly to build yk, then ykllvm clang via yk-config; Lua itself is built as gnu99
integration.thread_safety: The same as PUC Lua: one lua_State per thread. yk additionally runs trace compilation on YK_JOBS background threads (num_cpus - 1 by default).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial. The Lua 5.5.0 language and C API are unchanged, but the interpreter, and ideally the embedding host, must be compiled and linked with yk-config flags (fat LTO, all symbols exported to the dynamic table), and the full Lua test suite does not pass.

gotchas: Harness caveat on the timing: AWFY's harness.lua measures wall-clock time (os.monotonic), and yk compiles traces on up to num_cpus - 1 background threads (YK_JOBS default) on the 16-core EPYC 7F52. Stock Lua is single-threaded. CPU time is not reported, so the 1.96x is a wall-clock figure that does not charge JIT compilation. The suite also has no yklua executor with the JIT off (YK_JITC=none), so the cost of the yk instrumentation in interpreter mode is not shown.

The two binaries are built differently. The baseline is gcc -O2 -flto with Lua's computed-goto jump-table dispatch, which lvm.c enables by default under GCC. yklua is ykllvm clang -O2 with -DLUA_USE_JUMPTABLE=0, because yk cannot trace threaded dispatch. Results are correctness-checked: harness.lua asserts each benchmark's verification result. The cbgame inputs are scaled down from the standard sizes (fannkuchredux 10, binarytrees 15), and ReBench runs with --no-denoise.

Yk locations leak (issue #113, open since 2025-04): luaF_freeproto frees the yklocs array but never calls yk_location_drop. Programs that create functions repeatedly (load, string.dump and undump) therefore accumulate yk location state. The yklocs array is also not counted in luaF_protosize, so the GC does not account for it.

Warm-up is cheap but steady state is not always better. In the 2026-10-06 14:23 run, no benchmark's first iteration was more than 10% slower than its steady-state mean (iterations 6-10), and most were under 5% slower (DeltaBlue is the worst case, 793 ms against 720 ms). LuLPeg got slower as it ran (787 ms in iteration 1 against 911 ms over iterations 6-10, coefficient of variation 0.18; derived from page data).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: LuaJIT Remake (Deegen) and Luau target Lua 5.1 or a 5.1-derived dialect, and Pallene compiles a typed subset. yklua is the only catalogued option that JIT-compiles unmodified Lua 5.5, so pick it when you need 5.5 semantics and can accept pre-alpha status. For production embedding, Luau's interpreter or LuaJIT are the mature choices.
verified_claims_summary: yk's public ReBench harness (ykjit/yk-benchmarks) runs 22 benchmarks (14 AWFY, 4 CLBG, 3 real-world, BigLoop) for 5 invocations of 10 iterations each, on an AMD EPYC 7F52 (Debian, kernel 6.12.57). It compares yklua against stock PUC Lua 5.5.0 built with gcc -O2 -flto. I recomputed the 2026-10-06 14:23 run from its data file: a geomean time ratio of 0.511 (1.96x), with per-benchmark speedups from 1.09x (DeltaBlue) to 5.77x (Mandelbrot). The last 10 nightly runs range from 0.504 to 0.519.
status_note: Very active (a run of ltratt PRs merged 2026-10-05) but experimental and pre-alpha with 7 stars. The Lua core carries PUC-Rio's MIT notice and yk is Apache-2.0 or MIT, but the yklua repo has no LICENSE file covering its own changes, so treat it as a research artefact rather than something to vendor.
